historical_references.context: Najashi, the Christian King of Abyssinia, sent an embassy to the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) to inform him of his conversion to Islam and seek his blessings. Najashi's envoys were Abu Rafi', Ad-Dihy Al-Khawlani, and Al-Ajrad Al-Hudhali.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Hisham's Sirat Ibn Hisham, page 254 The name Najair carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) sent 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and Miqdad ibn Aswad to Najashi, the Christian King of Abyssinia, to invite him to Islam. They were received warmly and Najashi declared his faith in Islam, becoming known as Najashi Al-Akbar (Najashi the Great).

Overall, Najair represents a modern and culturally significant name with a rich history and meaning.
